prompt_en: Photorealistic square head-to-knees portrait of one clearly adult original woman in a flooded lunar archive refitted as a pressure-safe domestic study. In an adult restrained three-quarter view where both side contours remain visible, beside a glass cabinet she is decoding a palm-sized storm trapped inside it by aligning three copper tuning rings. A miniature aurora crosses her waist; glacial-cyan reflections rise from the flooded floor and contour her face. Her structured black-and-copper observatory uniform is practical, fully clothed, close-collared. Render a neutral hourglass silhouette relation: the upper torso expands above the waist around a comparatively narrower natural waist, then the hips expand below the waist; smooth transitions, pose viewpoint and garment cinching declared separately, fabric following form. Preserve stable facial appearance indicated by the reference image. In a slight three-quarter facial crop with soft form light across the upper lip, model the philtral contour as two philtral columns around a central philtral groove descending into a double upper-lip arc. Eye-level 50 mm, natural skin, wet reflections, smoke glass, oxidized copper, restrained haze; prioritize the storm interaction and aurora boundary.
negative_en: 3D render look, distorted fingers, over-processed retouching, cartoon style, unrealistic hands, broken facial features, low resolution, excessive HDR, body distortion

decisions.rationale: A cool adjacent lighting idea can be made diegetic through the frozen aurora and flooded floor.
decisions.artistic_interpretation: The blue-hour character becomes reflected lunar-interior light rather than an outdoor time-of-day cue.
decisions.transformation: The cool ambience is converted into a vertical bounce path from cyan water reflections onto the researcher's face.
decisions.prompt_evidence: glacial-cyan reflections rise from the flooded floor and contour her face

decisions.rationale: A distant complete-body view would reduce the facial and upper-lip resolution needed for the adopted profile.
A magazine treatment risks turning the instrument interaction into a posed fashion spread instead of a scientific event.
The frozen head-to-knees frame already balances face scale, hand action, and the waist-to-hip relation more effectively.
Motion trails would obscure precise facial surface anatomy and the mechanical alignment of the tuning rings.
The frozen photographic realism already supplies observation without importing a redundant documentary genre instruction.
